title: Flowboard: interactive autoscale playground & health strip for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an interactive 'Flowboard' view for Redwood Console focused on Dedicated GPU pools. The Flowboard combines a compact health strip, an autoscale playground (what-if simulator for autoscale policies and burst settings), and contextual rollout controls. Goals: 1) surface current health and SLO drift at-a-glance; 2) let operators simulate autoscale policy changes and see modeled latency/cost impact before applying; 3) provide safe canary/rollback controls tied to pool rollouts. Scope: health strip, simulator canvas, brief guidance copy, and an apply flow that triggers an infra proposal (RFC) to engineering. Acceptance criteria: high-fidelity Figma prototype linked, copy reviewed by PM, 3 scenarios for simulator (steady growth, sudden burst, KV-cache warm), usability test notes with 5 participants, engineering alignment on telemetry events and API hooks.

decisions: Ship the Flowboard as a read-write console panel behind a feature flag for Dedicated accounts only.
Simulator defaults to three presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with an Advanced toggle for fine-grained knobs.
Use amber/teal ops palette for transient warnings and healthy states; reserve red for hard failures only.
Cost estimates in the simulator will use a best-effort model and show a confidence band; exact billing remains in billing console.
Rollout actions require 2-step confirmation: apply + set rollback window (default 15 minutes).
Accessibility: keyboard-first controls and aria labels required before GA.
Telemetry contract agreed: simulator runs are logged and tied to pool id and user id for auditability (see GitHub PR for schema).
